s0758.literal: Close quotation. They mutually refuted and challenged; right and wrong were undecided, and Liu Chuo again retired.
s0758.idiomatic: They traded refutations until no decision was reached, and Liu Chuo again retired.

s0762.literal: Calendrical experts all praised its subtlety, and therefore its method is recorded here.
s0762.idiomatic: Calendrical experts praised its subtlety, and its method is recorded here.

s0783.literal: Each month add twenty greater intercalary decline units—this gives each month's intercalary decline.
s0783.idiomatic: Each month add 20 greater intercalary-decline units to obtain that month's intercalary decline.

s0784.literal: In general, the month establishing zi is the celestial first month; establishing chou is the terrestrial first month; establishing yin is the human first month.
s0784.idiomatic: The month establishing zi is the celestial first month; chou the terrestrial first month; yin the human first month.

s0789.literal: If the qi falls after midnight, measure the shadow using the following day as correct.
s0789.idiomatic: If the seasonal node falls after midnight, measure the shadow using the following day as the reference.

s0790.literal: For all additive operations, each subtracts its remainder from the divisor; what remains is the full remainder.
s0790.idiomatic: In additive operations, subtract each remainder from the divisor; the residue is the full remainder.

s0794.literal: In general, what does not complete a day is remainder; accumulated to form remainder is called a second.
s0794.idiomatic: Fractional parts of a day are remainders; accumulated remainders are called seconds.

s0795.literal: What does not complete a degree is a fraction; accumulated to form fractions is called a bamboo tally.
s0795.idiomatic: Fractional parts of a degree are fractions; accumulated fractions are called bamboo tallies.

s0796.literal: When seconds do not complete, they are called micro-units; when bamboo tallies do not complete, they are called minima.
s0796.idiomatic: Incomplete seconds are called micro-units; incomplete bamboo tallies are called minima.

s0806.literal: When the name has a total and day-degrees, full values, and fractions share a common term, addition and subtraction must be applied—all full values and shared fractions must be added or subtracted together.
s0806.idiomatic: When terms share totals, full day-degrees, and fractions, add or subtract all full values and shared fractions together.

s0807.literal: When multiplication is needed with fractions, the denominator must include the full value; after multiplication, divide back.
s0807.idiomatic: For multiplication with fractions, convert denominators to include full values; after multiplying, divide back.

s0808.literal: When fractions are combined with different denominators, multiply numerators and combine.
s0808.idiomatic: To combine fractions with different denominators, cross-multiply numerators and combine.

s0812.literal: When fractions have unequal denominators, convert to common terms: multiply this fraction by that denominator, then divide by this denominator to obtain that numerator.
s0812.idiomatic: When denominators differ, convert to common terms: multiply each fraction by the other's denominator, then divide to obtain the required numerator.

s0835.literal: Beyond the twelve chronograms is the remainder after zi-start.
s0835.idiomatic: Beyond the twelve chronograms lies the remainder after the start of zi.

s0837.literal: Four is lesser-greater, also called lesser.

s0841.literal: Eight is greater-lesser, also called greater.

s0848.literal: When initially forming eleven with a carry, it is called an exhausted chronogram.
s0848.idiomatic: When eleven is initially formed with a carry, it is called an exhausted chronogram.

s0860.literal: When prior entries are greater, add the total difference to the terminal rate—all become the qi-initial-day ascent-descent numbers.
s0860.idiomatic: When prior values are greater, add the total difference to the terminal rate to obtain each qi-initial-day ascent-descent value.

s0861.literal: By separate difference: when prior is greater subtract daily; when prior is less add to initial number—obtain each day's number.
s0861.idiomatic: By separate difference: subtract daily when prior is greater, add to the initial value when prior is less—yielding each day's value.

s0866.literal: When prior is less, within the limit self-multiply and multiply again by separate difference; self-multiply day-limit, double and divide; also add total rate—all become total numbers.
s0866.idiomatic: When prior is less: within the limit, square and multiply by the separate difference; square the day-limit, double and divide; add the total rate—all yielding total values.

s0872.literal: Also compute the next; add and count each in succession to obtain each fixed qi day and remainder.
s0872.idiomatic: Also compute the next entry; add and count in succession to obtain each fixed seasonal-node day and remainder.

s0873.literal: Also by prior and later already converted: subtract first, add later to the constant qi—this gives the next qi fixed day and remainder.
s0873.idiomatic: Using prior and later converted values: subtract first, then add to the constant qi to obtain the next fixed seasonal-node day and remainder.

s0878.literal: Divide the constant qi by three—each gives a mean pentad day.
s0878.idiomatic: Divide the constant qi by 3 to obtain each mean pentad day.

s0880.literal: Also compute the next; add and count each in succession to obtain the terminal pentad and next qi day.
s0880.idiomatic: Also compute the next; add and count in succession to obtain the terminal pentad and next seasonal-node day.

s0881.literal: Double the midnight clepsydra graduations to obtain night graduations.
s0881.idiomatic: Double the midnight clepsydra graduations to obtain night graduations.

s0882.literal: Subtract from one hundred graduations; what remains is day graduations.
s0882.idiomatic: Subtract from 100 graduations; the remainder is day graduations.

s0893.literal: Also for each pair of qi, daily increase is lesser.
s0893.idiomatic: For each pair of seasonal nodes, the daily increment decreases.

s0903.literal: Subtract from the upper position; what remains is what is added.
s0903.idiomatic: Subtract from the upper position; the remainder is the amount added.

s0904.literal: When not a full day, follow the chronogram rate.
s0904.idiomatic: When less than a full day, apply the chronogram rate.

s0931.literal: Also subtract the two limits to obtain limit decline.
s0931.idiomatic: Subtract the two limits to obtain the limit-decline value.

s0942.literal: Whether subtracting or not subtracting, the new-moon day tally matches the following month.
s0942.idiomatic: Whether subtracting or not, the new-moon day tally matches the following month.

s0943.literal: When neither has a standing tally, in a long month add the borrowed reduction tally after the fixed new-moon tally.
s0943.idiomatic: When neither has a standing tally, for a long month add the borrowed reduction tally after the fixed new-moon tally.

s0967.literal: When the Woman lodge ends connecting to Empty, this is called circuit fraction.
s0967.idiomatic: Where the Woman lodge ends connecting to Empty is called the circuit fraction.

s0978.literal: Prior entries are all equatorial degrees; their numbers are constant, girdling the celestial pole, the armillary standard.
s0978.idiomatic: Prior entries are equatorial degrees with constant values, girdling the celestial pole as the armillary standard.

s0999.literal: The moon and five planets enter and exit following this.
s0999.idiomatic: The moon and five planets enter and exit by this method.

s1007.literal: Still follow eleven increase-decrease to obtain later crossing and half-crossing numbers.
s1007.idiomatic: Apply the eleven-fold increase-decrease to obtain later crossing and half-crossing values.

s1009.literal: When the moon is outside, half after crossing before, decrease subtract increase add.
s1009.idiomatic: When the moon is outside, half after crossing before: apply decrease-subtract and increase-add.

s1010.literal: Half after crossing before, decrease add increase subtract on the ecliptic.
s1010.idiomatic: Half after crossing before: apply decrease-add and increase-subtract on the ecliptic.

s1014.literal: Accumulated crossing difference excess—follow crossing as standard.
s1014.idiomatic: When accumulated crossing difference is large, use the crossing as the standard.

s1029.literal: Remove the daily entry fraction from fixed new moon, accumulate increase-decrease to remove fixed new-moon days, then add fixed new-moon degree—also obtain midnight.
s1029.idiomatic: Remove daily entry fractions from the fixed new moon, accumulate increase-decrease, subtract fixed new-moon days, then add the fixed new-moon degree to obtain midnight position.

s1040.literal: Also multiply mean-conjunction remainder by degree standard, divide by approximation rate, subtract its chronogram position—for mean-conjunction midnight solar position.
s1040.idiomatic: Multiply mean-conjunction remainder by the degree standard, divide by the approximation rate, subtract the chronogram position—to obtain mean-conjunction midnight solar position.

s1057.literal: Following daily rotation, add fixed days to each to obtain new moon, quarter, and full-moon midnight lunar fixed degrees.
s1057.idiomatic: Following daily rotation, add fixed days to obtain new-moon, quarter, and full-moon midnight lunar fixed degrees.

s1066.literal: Subtract circuit fixed fraction for dusk fraction.
s1066.idiomatic: Subtract the circuit fixed fraction to obtain the dusk fraction.

s1067.literal: Divide for rotation degree; before full moon use dusk, after use dawn, add to midnight fixed degree—obtain position.
s1067.idiomatic: Divide for rotation degree; before full moon use dusk, after use dawn; add to midnight fixed degree to obtain position.

s1142.literal: New and full moon entry into crossing: if at limit or above, subtract crossing days; remainder is distance from later crossing.
s1142.idiomatic: At new or full moon entry into crossing: if at the limit or above, subtract crossing days; the remainder is distance from the later crossing.

s1168.literal: Before its fraction, also multiply the post-fraction qi count and add to after the fraction.
s1168.idiomatic: Before its fraction, multiply the post-fraction qi count and add to the value after the fraction.

s1180.literal: Within six qi adding two chronograms also follows the mean.
s1180.idiomatic: Within six seasonal nodes, adding two chronograms also follows the mean value.

s1190.literal: Although outside is full while the moon is below, inside loses while higher; shallow crossing then distant and idle.
s1190.idiomatic: Though outside appears full while the moon is below, inside loses height; shallow crossings appear distant.

s1195.literal: Assuming uniform winter and summer, morning and evening also differ.
s1195.idiomatic: Even assuming uniform winter and summer values, morning and evening observations differ.

s1196.literal: When positioned in southern chronograms the body is higher; east and west oblique viewing has skew.
s1196.idiomatic: In southern chronograms the body appears higher; oblique viewing from east and west introduces skew.

s1197.literal: Reason cannot be unified—because standard rates if true yet contradict.
s1197.idiomatic: The logic cannot be unified—standard rates, though seemingly correct, still contradict observation.

s1199.literal: If the location is not at Yangcheng, all gradually differ according to place.
s1199.idiomatic: Away from Yangcheng, all values gradually differ by location.

s1202.literal: Since the moon heralds sunlight, at noon it shines brighter; time also spans the earth—without abolishing received brightness.
s1202.idiomatic: Since the moon reflects sunlight, it shines brighter at noon; time also spans the earth without abolishing its received light.

s1214.literal: Then gen adds kun, xun subtracts qian from fixed remainder.
s1214.idiomatic: Then gen adds kun; xun subtracts qian from the fixed remainder.

s1237.literal: If due east, the moon descends obliquely north from above the sun.
s1237.idiomatic: Due east: the moon descends obliquely north from above the sun.

s1238.literal: Before the southeast corner, viewing eastward at first not direct—the moon high, sun below.
s1238.idiomatic: Before the southeast corner, viewing east: initially oblique—the moon high, sun below.

s1239.literal: Then the moon slightly northwest, sun gradually southeast; past the corner viewing south, moon more north, sun skewed southwest.
s1239.idiomatic: Then the moon shifts slightly northwest, the sun gradually southeast; past the corner viewing south, the moon more north, sun skewed southwest.

s1241.literal: After the southwest corner, viewing westward, moon is northeast, sun southwest.
s1241.idiomatic: After the southwest corner, viewing west: moon northeast, sun southwest.

s1252.literal: Due east, the moon reflects obliquely south from below the sun.
s1252.idiomatic: Due east: the moon reflects obliquely south from below the sun.

s1253.literal: North of the corner, then moon slightly southeast, sun returns west.
s1253.idiomatic: North of the corner: moon slightly southeast, sun returns west.

s1255.literal: North of the corner, moon has southwest, sun again northeast.
s1255.idiomatic: North of the corner: moon southwest, sun again northeast.

s1256.literal: Due west, the moon rises obliquely south from below the sun.
s1256.idiomatic: Due west: the moon rises obliquely south from below the sun.

s1380.literal: When prior adds degrees, subtract according to this.
s1380.idiomatic: When prior entries add degrees, subtract accordingly.

s1437.literal: All divide by bamboo-tally divisor for rotation fraction.
s1437.idiomatic: All divide by the bamboo-tally divisor to obtain rotation fraction.

s1438.literal: What remains is still called bamboo tally—each gives daily position knowing distance from sun degree.
s1438.idiomatic: Remainders are still called bamboo tallies—each gives the daily position and distance from the sun.

s1439.literal: Increase by daily entry prior-later fraction to fix it.
s1439.idiomatic: Increase by the daily entry prior-later fraction to obtain the fixed value.

s1443.literal: For Venus and Mars day-degrees, compute count increase-decrease to fix them.
s1443.idiomatic: For Venus and Mars day-degrees, compute increase-decrease counts to obtain fixed values.

s1449.literal: What does not complete is also called bamboo tally.
s1449.idiomatic: Incomplete values are also called bamboo tallies.

s0428.literal: When full counts as days; remainder is day fraction; add days from new moon since entering qi; remove and count as before.
s0428.idiomatic: When full counts as days; remainder is day fraction; add days from new moon since entering qi; remove and count as before.

s0430.literal: When day fraction fills submergence divisor, carry to days; remove and count as before.
s0430.idiomatic: When day fraction fills submergence divisor, carry to days; remove and count as before.

s0437.literal: To find the next month: add 1 day and remainder 2,486, small fraction 21; when full remove as before—this gives next month calendar entry day and remainder.
s0437.idiomatic: To find the next month: add 1 day and remainder 2,486, small fraction 21; when full remove as before—this gives next month calendar entry day and remainder.

s0438.literal: To find full moon: add 14 days, remainder 1,949, small fraction 21½; when full remove as before—this gives full-moon calendar entry day and remainder.
s0438.idiomatic: To find full moon: add 14 days, remainder 1,949, small fraction 21½; when full remove as before—this gives full-moon calendar entry day and remainder.

s0441.literal: Divide by difference divisor together with entering-qi fixed anomaly; all apply expansion-subtract and contraction-add to base new/full moon small remainder.
s0441.idiomatic: Divide by difference divisor together with entering-qi fixed anomaly; all apply expansion-subtract and contraction-add to base new/full moon small remainder.

s0468.literal: Remove and count as before; when passing Dipper remove 10 rotation fractions and 466 small fractions.
s0468.idiomatic: Remove and count as before; when passing Dipper remove 10 rotation fractions and 466 small fractions.

s0470.literal: Multiply midnight calendar-entry day remainder by rotation difference; divide by circuit divisor to obtain one—this is variation difference; advance-add and retreat-subtract to daily rotation fraction for fixed fraction.
s0470.idiomatic: Multiply midnight calendar-entry day remainder by rotation difference; divide by circuit divisor to obtain one—this is variation difference; advance-add and retreat-subtract to daily rotation fraction for fixed fraction.

s0492.literal: For Venus and Mercury, subtract evening appearance-disappearance days; the remainder is evening mean-appearance day and fraction.
s0492.idiomatic: For Venus and Mercury, subtract evening appearance-disappearance days; the remainder is evening mean-appearance day and fraction.

s0523.literal: Mercury: morning mean appearance before Start of Summer and after Rain Water—should appear but does not.
s0523.idiomatic: Mercury: morning mean appearance before Start of Summer and after Rain Water—should appear but does not.

s0524.literal: From Awakening of Insects through Rain Water, 18° to 46° from the sun—in the morning, if Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, or Venus is present, it appears.
s0524.idiomatic: From Awakening of Insects through Rain Water, 18° to 46° from the sun—in the morning, if Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, or Venus is present, it appears.

s0526.literal: From Start of Summer through Lesser Fullness, solar distance as before—in the morning, if one or more of Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, or Venus is present, it appears.
s0526.idiomatic: From Start of Summer through Lesser Fullness, solar distance as before—in the morning, if one or more of Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, or Venus is present, it appears.

s0530.literal: Evening mean appearance after End of Heat and before Frost Descent—should appear but does not.
s0530.idiomatic: Evening mean appearance after End of Heat and before Frost Descent—should appear but does not.

s0650.literal: Remainder below full-moon difference and above outer limit—at full moon there is lunar eclipse.
